title: Baker Mayfield's 198.9 Passing Efficiency Record (2017)
question: What was Baker Mayfield's record passing efficiency rating at Oklahoma?
answer: Baker Mayfield posted a 198.9 passing efficiency rating in 2017, breaking his own FBS single-season record of 196.4 from 2016. Oklahoma teammate Kyler Murray later topped it with a 199.2 in 2018.
summary: Baker Mayfield's 198.9 rating in 2017 broke his own 196.4 FBS record from 2016. See the numbers and how Kyler Murray passed it in 2018.
body: Passing efficiency is the formula the NCAA uses to rate quarterbacks, folding completion percentage, yardage, touchdowns and interceptions into a single number. Baker Mayfield pushed that number to heights college football had never seen while leading the Sooners.

His 2016 season produced a rating of 196.4, an FBS single-season record at that time. A year later, in 2017, he topped himself. Mayfield finished with a 198.9 rating, which the Davey O'Brien Award site describes as breaking his own all-time NCAA record. He completed 285 of 404 passes, a 70.5 percent clip, for 4,627 yards and 43 touchdowns, both second nationally that season. That year he also won the Heisman Trophy.

Records in this category do not sit still. Kyler Murray, who followed Mayfield as Oklahoma's starter, posted a 199.2 rating in 2018. In that same season Alabama's Tua Tagovailoa finished with a 199.4. Later quarterbacks pushed the mark higher still, so Mayfield no longer holds the top spot.

Even so, Oklahoma quarterbacks hold three of the best single-season ratings in the FBS record book: Mayfield's 196.4 and 198.9, and Murray's 199.2. It is a good measure of how productive the Sooner offense was in the Lincoln Riley era.
